LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 MODAL AUXILIARIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words do we use to express requests, permission, ability and obligation?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify modal auxiliaries in a passage
2. use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods
3. value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 MODAL AUXILIARIES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 3.3.1 MODAL AUXILIARIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify modal auxiliaries in a passage

What this means
In this part you learn to identify modal auxiliaries in a passage. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify modal auxiliaries in a passage.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify modal auxiliaries in a passage. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods

What this means
In this part you learn to use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify modal auxiliaries in a passage)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries to a partner. (skill: use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify modal auxiliaries in a passage.
3. Practise this skill: use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods.
4. Practise this skill: value the importance of using modal auxiliaries in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use to express requests, permission, ability and obligation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 3.3.1 Modal Auxiliaries means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify modal auxiliaries in a passage.
5. Be able to: use modal auxiliaries in sentences to express different moods.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
